To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 77 GHz FMCW front end can be implemented using a low cost 65 nm CMOS technology, that the FPGA can be used to implement the beamforming algorithm and that a DSP can be used to reconstruct the radar image.

the 77-GHz front-end with FPGA support is capable of processing the received signals from a 2x2 receive antenna array and that a 2x1 synthetic aperture can be used to reconstruct the reflectance of the imaging area.
the proposed radar system has a high potential for automotive applications and can be used for imaging applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a 77 GHz FMCW radar front-end for automotive applications.
the development of a low cost radar front-end with FPGA support for automotive applications.
the development of a radar front-end with FPGA, DSP, and analog support.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented radar system can be considered as a first step towards an affordable and compact automotive radar front-end with FPGA- and DSP-based digital array processing capabilities.
the system is able to perform a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) measurement with an angular resolution of 0.1°.
the presented prototype radar is able to perform the imaging task with a resolution of about 1 m and an angular accuracy of 0.5 degrees.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that it is possible to implement the radar front end with the FPGA and DSP support and the system is capable of processing the received data and generating the reflectivity map in real time.

the system is capable of imaging objects with a resolution better than 10 cm at a distance of about 10 m.
A 77-GHZ FMCW RADAR FRONT-END WITH FPGA AND DSP
the presented radar system is capable of processing up to eight parallel receive channels in real-time and is able to reconstruct a reflectivity map with an angular resolution of 1.5 degrees.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of an FPGA and a DSP is a promising approach for future radar systems.
FPGAs can handle the data processing of the radar signal and the DSP can handle the computationally intensive algorithms.
FMCW systems with a high sampling rate are suitable for the realization of radar systems with high resolution.
